Triggers.value: Being in a natural environment similar to where it happened

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
I wake during the night to check whether I am safe
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory
There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try
Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel like I don't know myself anymore
Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
I can't rely on other people

issues.item: Triggers: Crash Imagery: Cars hit by accident
issues.explanation: 'Crash Imagery: Cars hit by accident' is hard to reconcile with the validated trauma type of natural disaster. A car-crash-specific trigger suggests a different index trauma unless there is clear disaster-related context, which is not reflected elsewhere in the profile.

issues.item: Memory: Rage on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense rage
issues.explanation: 'Rage on Recall' is not well supported by the rest of the profile, which otherwise centers on fear, vulnerability, dissociation/gaps, and interpersonal mistrust after a natural disaster. Intense rage could occur clinically, but here it lacks corroboration from threat or appraisal items and weakens overall coherence.

For a natural disaster trauma, 'related people' as a primary trigger is hard to justify unless they were directly linked to the event; with no supporting interpersonal trauma content elsewhere, this trigger is clinically questionable.

issues.item: Threat: Threat in Silence: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen
issues.explanation: The threat item about unusual silence implying imminent danger fits combat/interpersonal danger contexts more than natural disaster exposure, and it is not supported by the trigger or appraisal content here.

vignette: Lukas had always loved the outdoors, spending countless hours hiking and camping in the mountains of Colorado where he grew up. But all of that changed on a fateful day three years ago when a devastating wildfire swept through his favorite trail, forcing him to flee for his life. Lukas remembered the sound of crackling flames, the feeling of ash raining down on him, and the sight of trees exploding into fireballs. He recalled running as fast as he could, his lungs burning from the smoke, but the details after that were hazy. As the days turned into weeks, Lukas began to feel a growing sense of unease whenever he found himself in natural environments similar to where the wildfire occurred. A trip to a park or a walk through the woods would suddenly transport him back to that terrifying day, and he'd feel like he was reliving the experience all over again. He started avoiding outdoor activities altogether, opting instead for the safety of his car or the confines of his apartment. But even in these supposedly safe spaces, Lukas couldn't shake off the feeling of vulnerability that had settled deep within him. He'd wake up in the middle of the night to check whether he was truly alone, his heart racing at the slightest creak of the floorboards. During the day, he found himself perpetually on guard, scanning his surroundings for potential threats – a habit that made him feel like he was constantly "on edge." His friends and family began to notice the change in him, commenting on how jumpy and irritable he'd become. Lukas tried to brush off their concerns, but deep down, he knew something was wrong. He couldn't remember certain parts of the wildfire incident, no matter how hard he tried – it was as if his mind had deliberately erased those moments from his memory. And whenever he did recall fragments of that day, he'd feel a wave of terror wash over him, just like he had during the actual event. As time went on, Lukas started to question his own identity and sense of purpose. He used to be an adventurous person, always looking for the next thrill or challenge – but now he felt lost and rudderless. Nothing seemed meaningful anymore; even his job as a salesperson, which had once brought him satisfaction, now felt hollow and unfulfilling. Lukas couldn't help but wonder if he was truly alone in this feeling of despair. He started to withdraw from social interactions, fearing that others wouldn't understand what he was going through – or worse, that they'd judge him for his weakness. His relationships began to suffer as a result; friends and family members tried to reach out to him, but Lukas pushed them away, convinced that no one could be trusted. One night, after yet another sleepless episode spent checking the locks on his door and scanning the shadows outside, Lukas finally hit rock bottom. He realized he couldn't keep living like this – constantly on edge, afraid of his own emotions, and disconnected from the world around him. With a mix of trepidation and determination, he made an appointment with a therapist, hoping that someone might be able to help him unravel the tangled mess within himself.
